title: Tips for Your Buttons
summary: Read a button's tip, say what its drag does in your own words, add a message, and choose how much Kneady says.

steps.title: Step 1: Read Turn's Tip
text: 1. Rest the mouse on Turn on the mannequin's head. After half a second its tip shows under its name.
2. In the tree, click the arrow beside Head, then click Turn.
3. At the end of Turn's settings, click Tip to open it.
A tip has a row per key: the key on the left, what it does on the right. Kneady writes both from the button's commands, so a tip stays true when they change. The rows under Tip are the tip's own.

media.label: On the head, then in the Kneady tab

steps.title: Step 2: Say It Your Way
text: 1. In the Drag ↔ row, click the field holding Kneady's words in grey, type Turn the head and press Enter.
2. Rest the mouse on Turn: its tip says yours.

Your words stay with the row - the left and right drag - not its place, so they keep if the commands change, and the status bar says them too. Clear the field to go back to Kneady's. The eye beside a row hides it from the tip.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the head

steps.title: Step 3: Add a Message
text: 1. Click the field under the rows, type Looks left and right. and press Enter.
2. Rest the mouse on Turn: the message shows under a line.
The rows say what the keys do; the message says what the button is for. A copied button takes its tip with it.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the head

steps.title: Step 4: How Much Kneady Says
text: 1. At the top of the Kneady tab, set Help to Inform.
2. Rest the mouse on Turn: its tip shows your drag row and your message, and leaves out Ctrl and Shift.

Learn shows every key; Inform leaves the keys every button shares to the status bar; Quiet shows no tips. Help is yours, not the file's: it follows you into every file. Set it back to Learn for the tutorials.

media.label: In the Kneady tab, then on the head
